subject: biology
title: Levels of organisation
key_idea: Living things are built in levels. Cells make up tissues, tissues make up organs, and organs work together in organ systems. Organ systems together make up the whole organism.

blocks.text: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living organisms. This section covers each level and how they fit together.

items.meaning: The basic building block of all living organisms.
A group of cells with a similar structure and function.
A group of different tissues working together to do a specific job.
A group of organs working together to do a job for the whole body.
A living thing, made of organ systems working together.

diagram.alt: The levels of organisation in order: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism. Each level is made of the one before.

items: Cells make tissues. Tissues make organs. Organs make organ systems.
A tissue is a group of cells with a similar function.
An organ is made of different tissues.

blocks.text: Every level has examples you need to be able to name. Animals and plants are organised in the same way.

items: The heart is an organ. It is made of different tissues, such as muscle tissue, that perform specific functions.
Other animal organs include the brain, lungs, liver, kidney, stomach, intestines, pancreas and skin.
The heart is part of the circulatory system.
The digestive system is an organ system. Several organs work together to digest and absorb food.
A leaf is an organ. A root is an organ. The stem is an organ.
Spongy mesophyll and xylem are tissues.
The heart, lungs, liver and kidney are organs. Blood is not an organ.
A leaf and a root are plant organs. Spongy mesophyll and xylem are tissues.
The size order runs nucleus, cell, tissue, organ.

blocks.text: Exam questions ask you to put structures in order of size. Each level is made of the level before it, so it is always larger.

diagram.alt: Put the structures in order of size, smallest first.
diagram.prompt: Put these in order, smallest to largest

items: A nucleus is inside a cell, so a cell is larger.
Work up the levels one at a time: cell, tissue, organ, organ system.

checks.a: A group of cells with a similar structure and function.

checks.q: Why is the heart described as an organ?
checks.a: It is made up of different tissues that perform specific functions.

checks.q: Write these in order of size, smallest first: cell, nucleus, organ, tissue.

exam_phrases: a group of the same / similar cells
a group of cells with a (similar / specific) function
a group of tissues working together is an organ
it is made up of (different) tissues that perform specific functions

mistakes.wrong: A tissue is a group of cells.
mistakes.right: "A group of cells" on its own is ignored. Say a group of the same or similar cells, or a group of cells with a similar function.

mistakes.wrong: The heart is part of the blood system.
mistakes.right: "Blood system" is ignored. Say the circulatory system (cardiovascular is also accepted).

mistakes.wrong: The root hair cell is the plant organ that absorbs water from the soil.
mistakes.right: "Root hair" is not accepted. The organ is the root.
"Blood" is ignored when naming an organ. Name the heart, lung, liver, kidney, brain, stomach, intestine, pancreas, bladder or skin.

worked_example.question:
